_comment: Extent tracker (v0). Which downloaded base polygons are highlighted, by the NAME the base map gives them in each era, bounded by start/end years. The polygons themselves are never edited. Rows in data/records.csv with tracker=extent can add to or override this list. An entry with `stages` lights by default only on those stages (an empty list: only when ?focus= names it), so the Europe stage's states (2026-11-09) leave every other stage's map as it was; `label` is what the map prints, which may differ from the base map's own name (historical-basemaps calls the Habsburg lands 'Austrian Empire' before 1804 and Great Britain 'United Kingdom' in 1715).
title: Extent of states

highlights.label: Spain
highlights._why: From Charles I (1516), who ruled Castile and Aragon together; historical-basemaps names the polygon Spain from its 1530 map (Castile before).

highlights.label: Habsburg Monarchy
highlights._why: From 1526 (Bohemia and Hungary to the Habsburgs). historical-basemaps names these lands 'Austrian Empire', a title first used in 1804; the label says Habsburg Monarchy. Its 1700 map has only Hungary and its neighbors in that polygon (Austria and Bohemia are inside the Holy Roman Empire's); its 1715 map has all three.

highlights.label: Prussia
highlights._why: From 1618, when Brandenburg's elector inherited the Duchy of Prussia. historical-basemaps draws Brandenburg (subject of Prussia) apart only from its 1715 map; before that Brandenburg is inside the Holy Roman Empire's polygon and only the duchy is lit.

highlights.label: England
highlights._why: Lit only when an order names it (?focus=england): the constitutional contrast for an absolutism lesson. historical-basemaps' 'England and Ireland' (1530–1700) is labeled England.

highlights.label: Great Britain
highlights._why: Lit only when an order names it (?focus=britain). From the Union of 1707; historical-basemaps' 1715 map calls it 'United Kingdom', a name first used in 1801, so the label says Great Britain.

highlights.label: Dutch Republic
highlights._why: Lit only when an order names it (?focus=dutch-republic): the republican contrast.

_cliopatria: 2026-11-09: the world page draws its states from Cliopatria (src/render/states.js), so each entry also lists the names Cliopatria gives the state (checked against its rows: Safavid Dynasty 1502-1737 Q161205, Ming Dynasty 1375-1644 Q9903, Qing Dynasty 1645-1911 Q8733, Marinid Sultanate 1250-1467 Q582861, Wattasid dynasty 1468-1555 Q970799, Kingdom of Spain 1516- Q29, Brandenburg-Prussia 1619-1720 Q157367, Kingdom of Sweden Q34, Swedish Empire 1612-1814 Q215443, Commonwealth of England 1645-1661 Q330362, Grand Principality of Moscow 1294-1546 Q170770; the rest share the base maps' names). On the political map every state is colored; an entry gives a state its name of the time and lets ?focus= pick it; `stages` now matters only to the admin page and the Diff view's tracked scope.
